title: Intermittent Transcranial Brain Stimulation of the Temporo-parietal Junction: A Proof-of-concept Study to Reduce Aggression in Violent Delinquency
summary: The main objective of the study is to investigate the efficacy of non-invasive brain stimulation in reducing aggressive behavior (reactive and reward-related) and increasing empathy in offenders by comparing TPJ versus vertex (control site) stimulation. The focus is on biological, neurological and behavioral characteristics of aggression. Offenders and controls without a violent criminal background are investigated.
conditions: Offenders with and without mental disorders, including personality disorders and substance abuse, are included in this group due to their high prevalence.
